title: I developed the game to find the clones of Needle In A Haystack Simulator, entirely with AI
author: Daniele-Fantastico
selftext:
Do you know the game *Needle In A Haystack Simulator* and the dozens upon dozens of clones released these days? They made me think of developing a game where you have to find the original game among millions of clones. Obviously they will clone this one too, but anyway it was mostly fun and an experiment.

Title: **Needle in a Haystack Simulator in a Haystack of Needle in a Haystack Simulators**

The game was made entirely with AI. Specifically with Claude Code and ChatGPT’s Imagegen. All in less than 6 days.

A few numbers to give you an idea of the effort:  
\- developed in Unity (with MCP for Unity)  
\- 60 commits  
\- 34,000 lines of C# (I haven’t read a single one)  
\- music and sound effects synthesized by code (4,400 lines of code)  
\- 3D models made by Claude, generated by editor scripts  
\- 32 images generated by Claude via image\_gen (Claude Code has access to the Codex CLI)  
\- A lot of SVGs generated by Claude for the gameplay  
\- The fonts are the only thing not created by AI!  
\- approximately 7 million tokens used (with Max 5x subscription)

The sessions (and related prompts) were very many. From the first prototype to the finished game it was continuous work for all 6 days. The changes to gameplay, graphics, and balancing were huge. In 6 days I was able to test lots of different options, looking for the feeling I liked best.

Even the trailer was made by Claude!

During the waits, sometimes even long ones, I did many other things on our “real” projects.

In the end, even for the Steam page, I had Claude do everything, through its internal browser. It configured and uploaded everything, all by itself.

I only used Opus 5.5, Max and Extra effort. Almost never reached the 5h limit.

It was all very fun!

If you have any questions, if you want any "development" details, feel free to ask.

Thanks.
